from.place: clause 4: '$F$ is exact (it commutes with finite limits and finite colimits)'

title: Exact functor
statement: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor. $F$ *commutes with* (preserves) a limit (resp. colimit) of a diagram $M:\mathcal I\to\mathcal A$ if it carries a limit cone (resp. colimit cocone) of $M$ to a limit cone (resp. colimit cocone) of $F\circ M$. If $\mathcal A$ has finite limits ([def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]), $F$ is *left exact* if it commutes with all finite limits; if $\mathcal A$ has finite colimits, $F$ is *right exact* if it commutes with all finite colimits; $F$ is *exact* if it is both left and right exact.

source.place: Categories, Definition 0034 (label definition-exact), in Section 0033 (label section-exact-functor)
